title: Skillet Zucchini with Parmesan
description: Tender golden zucchini finished with Parmesan for an easy vegetable side that takes about 15 minutes.
substitutions: Use yellow summer squash for some or all of the zucchini.
Use nutritional yeast instead of Parmesan for a dairy-free finish.
Italian seasoning can replace the garlic powder.

steps.text: Slice 2 medium zucchini into about 1/2-inch half-moons so they cook quickly without turning mushy.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil or butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the zucchini in a fairly even layer. Sprinkle with 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp black pepper.
Cook 6 to 8 minutes, stirring only every couple of minutes, until the zucchini is tender with browned edges.
Turn off the heat. Sprinkle with 1/4 cup grated Parmesan and optional 1 tsp lemon juice. Toss once and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet for the best texture.

title: Maple Roasted Sweet Potatoes
description: Caramelized roasted sweet potato cubes with a light maple-butter glaze—simple, cozy, and not overly sweet.
substitutions: Use brown sugar instead of maple syrup.
Use all olive oil instead of butter if preferred.
Pumpkin pie spice can replace the cinnamon.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan if you want easier cleanup.
Cut 2 lb sweet potatoes into roughly 1-inch cubes so they roast at the same rate.
Toss the sweet potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 1 tbsp melted butter, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp cinnamon, and optional pinch cayenne.
Spread the sweet potatoes in one layer on the sheet pan with a little room between pieces.
Roast 15 minutes, then turn the pieces with a spatula.
Roast 12 to 15 minutes more, until browned at the edges and easily pierced with a fork.
Taste and add a small pinch more salt if needed. Serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a hot oven, skillet, or air fryer to restore browned edges.

title: Buttery Corn & Peppers
description: Sweet corn and colorful peppers cooked quickly in butter for a bright, inexpensive side dish.

ingredients.notes: frozen and thawed, canned and drained, or fresh

substitutions: Use olive oil instead of butter.
Add a handful of diced zucchini if it needs using up.

steps.text: Dice 1 medium bell pepper into small pieces.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the diced bell pepper and cook about 3 minutes, until it starts to soften.
Add 3 cups corn, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, and optional 1/4 tsp smoked paprika.
Cook 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the corn is hot and gets a few lightly browned spots.
Turn off the heat and stir in optional parsley or green onion. Serve hot.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet or microwave.

title: One-Pot Sausage Tomato Orzo
description: A cozy one-pot dinner with browned sausage, tender orzo, tomatoes, and spinach in a lightly creamy sauce.
equipment: large deep skillet or Dutch oven
substitutions: Use turkey or chicken sausage instead of pork sausage.
Use chopped kale instead of spinach; simmer it a few minutes longer.

steps.text: Put 12 oz Italian sausage in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Break it into small pieces and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until browned and no pink remains.
If there is more than about 1 tbsp fat in the pan, spoon off the extra.
Stir in 1 cup dry orzo and 1/2 tsp Italian seasoning. Cook 1 minute so the orzo is coated in the pan juices.
Add 1 can diced tomatoes with juices and 2 cups chicken broth. Stir well and scrape any browned bits from the bottom.
Bring to a gentle simmer, then lower the heat to medium-low. Cook 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes so the orzo does not stick, until tender and saucy.
Stir in 2 cups baby spinach and optional 1/4 cup cream. Cook 1 to 2 minutes, until the spinach wilts.
Turn off the heat and stir in 1/4 cup grated Parmesan. Taste before adding extra salt because sausage, broth, and Parmesan are already salty.
Let the orzo stand 2 minutes to thicken slightly, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. The orzo thickens as it sits; loosen leftovers with a splash of broth or water while reheating.
